title: Safe Door Edge and Strike Area (Toolmark Check)
prompt:
1) Function (1 sentence)
Create a forensic-quality close-up color photograph documenting potential toolmarks on a safe door edge and strike/bolt area for comparison and examination.

2) Scene / Composition (3–5 sentences; include subject percentage in frame)
A tight close-up shows the vertical edge of a matte dark-gray safe door meeting the lighter gray strike plate/receiver area on the frame, with the seam/edge and strike zone centered. The suspected toolmark region (fine linear scratches and small nicks) is visible along the door edge and around the strike opening, illuminated with raking light to emphasize surface relief. A small, plain forensic scale (neutral, unbranded, black-and-white mm markings) is placed adjacent to the toolmarks without covering them. Include a minimal annotation label card within the frame (no case name), with handwritten-style text limited to “Evidence: ev_safe_door_edge_toolmarks_003” and “Photo: 003”. The safe edge/strike area occupies ~70% of the frame, scale and annotation card together ~15%, background metal surface ~15%.

3) Angle & Distance (strict numeric values)
Angle: 20° off perpendicular (camera tilted 20° from a straight-on view to the surface plane). Distance: 0.35 m from lens to the toolmark area.

4) Optics & Technique (lens mm, f/, 1/x s, ISO, WB K, focus, DOF)
Lens: 60 mm macro; aperture f/11; shutter 1/125 s; ISO 200; white balance 5000K. Focus locked on the midpoint of the toolmark cluster; deep enough DOF to keep the scale markings legible and the strike edge sharp. Technique: single exposure, even color, high detail, minimal noise; raking light from camera-left at ~15° grazing angle to reveal striations.

5) Mandatory elements (labels/markers/timestamps already present in the case)
Include only: the forensic scale (mm), and an annotation card reading exactly “Evidence: ev_safe_door_edge_toolmarks_003” and “Photo: 003”.

6) Negatives (objective list of what MUST NOT appear)
No people, hands, fingerprints, or faces. No brands, logos, serial numbers, or identifiable manufacturer markings. No caseId or evidence title text inside the image beyond the specified annotation card text. No timestamps, no police/official badges, no real addresses, no license plates. No blood, weapons, or graphic violence. No additional labels like “CAM-##”, no extra evidence tags, no rulers other than the single plain scale.

7) Acceptance checklist (objective, verifiable bullets)
- Close-up color photo of safe door edge and strike/receiver area with visible fine scratches/nicks consistent with toolmark examination.
- Raking light clearly emphasizes surface relief and striations without blown highlights.
- One plain mm scale is present and legible, placed adjacent to (not covering) the suspected marks.
- One annotation card present with exactly the specified two lines of text and no other identifiers.
- No brands/logos/serial numbers, no people, no timestamps, no extra labels.
- Image is sharp, forensic-quality, and shows the toolmark region occupying ~70% of the frame.
